title: Automatic session titles and continuation lineage
contract: Two stages with a provenance ladder: `derive_title()` names the session from the first user message *before the model is called* — free, deterministic, capped at 48 chars on a word boundary (measured p50 151 s / p90 1212 s of nameless sessions before this existed) — then one small-model call upgrades it, constrained by a strict `json_schema` `{"title": string}` with `additionalProperties: false`, which eliminated the whole class of "model answered the prompt instead of titling it" failures. Input capped at 1,000 chars. Fires once per session, never overwrites a human title. Compression continuations get `base #2`, `base #3` via `get_next_title_in_lineage`, carry `parent_session_id`, are hidden from pickers, and resolve to the newest member when resumed by name. (memory.session-auto-title, title-lineage)
governance: read-only (metadata on the user's own session); one auxiliary model call, local by default

title: Getting back into a conversation: continue, resume, and a free recap
contract: `-c`/`--continue` resolves through a per-terminal breadcrumb (tty, tmux pane, kitty window, wezterm pane, Zellij pane, Windows Terminal session) expiring at 30 days, so two panes side by side each continue their own conversation instead of both grabbing the globally newest; `--resume` accepts id, unique prefix, title, `latest`, `@claude` or `@codex`. On resume a styled "Previous Conversation" panel replays the last 10 exchanges — user turns gold `●`, assistant green `◆`, tool calls collapsed to `[3 tool calls: terminal, web_search]` — with **no LLM call**. `/recap` does the same for the live session from the in-memory transcript, again with no model call, deliberately: an LLM-generated recap costs a cache miss and adds latency for no accuracy gain. (memory.session-resume, resume-recap, session-recap)

title: Undoing what the agent did to the filesystem
contract: A single shared bare git store at `~/.hermes/checkpoints/store/` with per-project refs, indexes and metadata, driven through `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` so no git state leaks into the user's directory and objects deduplicate across worktrees (the pre-v2 per-project design burned ~40 MB per worktree). It snapshots **before `write_file`, before `patch`, and before destructive terminal commands** — `rm`, `mv`, `sed -i`, `dd`, `truncate`, `shred`, `>` redirects, `git reset/clean/checkout` — at most once per directory per turn, never raising. An agent-write ledger records the sha256 of every file Hermes wrote, so `/rollback <N>` restores while **skipping files you edited yourself** and naming them; `--all` overrides, `diff <N>` previews, `<N> <file>` restores one file, and a pre-rollback snapshot makes the undo itself undoable. Opt-in (`checkpoints.enabled: false`), size-capped, auto-pruned. (memory.checkpoints-store, rollback, cli-checkpoints-status, prune, clear, clear-legacy, api-checkpoints)
governance: Already correct for file writes — `file.write` with a mandatory snapshot precondition. Extending to shell makes the snapshot a precondition of `terminal.exec` too (registry.py:114); restore is itself a privileged write and must re-enter through the same kind, never as a side door.

title: The post-turn learning loop that decides what is worth remembering
contract: `auxiliary.background_review` forks after a turn and replays the conversation, by default on the main chat model so the prompt cache is warm; pointing it at a cheaper model automatically switches to a compact digest replay (recent turns verbatim + a summary of older ones) for ~3–5× lower cost with near-identical capture. It runs with its own tool whitelist (memory, skill management, read-only file tools; `extra_tools` opts in more but cannot enable anything the parent lacks), its own usage accounting (`session_model_usage` rows tagged `task='background_review'`), and nudge intervals zeroed inside the fork so the review cannot nudge itself. `display.memory_notifications: off|on|verbose` controls only the chat line — turning it off does not turn off the writes; `memory.write_approval` is the gate for that. (memory.background-review, review-notifications)
governance: Its skill legs already cross quarantine and the approval queue. Its memory leg is the specific writer that row 3's `memory.write` kind must gate first — the highest-volume autonomous writer in the system.
remaining_verbatim:
- Every channel conversation, the owner's own Telegram or Slack DM included, is always held for approval. An inbound channel is untrusted, so its conversation never reaches the clean list (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1671-1672, agents/core/learning/review_policy.py:330-341). Hermes writes from a platform DM unless memory.write_approval is on. The approval dial on ask also holds a clean HUD turn's writes (agents/core/learning/review_policy.py:136-137).
- extra_tools and nudge-zeroing inside the review fork were not verified. Nerva's review is one structured call with no tool loop, so it has no fork whitelist to extend and no nudge counter to zero, and neither Hermes behaviour has a tested counterpart.

title: Reading documents into the conversation
contract: `read_file` on a document path converts to Markdown: `.ipynb`/`.docx`/`.xlsx` via built-in stdlib converters (always available), and `.pdf`, legacy Office, OpenDocument, `.rtf`/`.epub` via an optional lazily-installed converter, paginated through the normal `offset`/`limit` window and working across remote terminal backends (bytes cross the boundary, conversion happens host-side). The valuable part is detecting the silent failure: when a PDF's text layer yields nothing on >20% of pages or 10+ pages absolute, it prepends a structured coverage warning listing each gap as `pages <a>-<b> — after "<last text>"`, telling the agent to target only the gaps it needs rather than OCR everything. Documents over 50 MB are refused. (memory.document-extraction)
governance: read-only, but extracted text enters the transcript and therefore the context budget and the store — it must pass the same scan as any other untrusted ingest
remaining_verbatim:
- **Formats:** file_read still extracts only .pdf and .docx (agents/core/file_tools.py:202). There is no .ipynb, .xlsx, legacy Office, OpenDocument, .rtf or .epub reading, and no Markdown conversion beyond DOCX table rows.
- **Parser memory:** peak parser memory and CPU are not bounded. pypdf and python-docx load the whole admitted input, up to 50 MB, and the budgets cap only the extracted text and the wall clock between pages or blocks.
- **Coverage gaps:**
  - No OCR is performed by file_read; optional Workspace OCR is separate and still lacks real-engine/platform acceptance.
  - The garbled-text heuristic cannot catch well-formed but wrong text.
  - DOCX equations are counted but not extracted.
  - DOCX comments and tracked deletions are not reported.
- **Indexer:** the local_docs bulk indexer still reads body paragraphs only (agents/core/local_docs.py:563).

title: Process heap trimming for long-lived agent processes
contract: `context.memory_trim` calls `malloc_trim(0)` through ctypes on Linux/glibc to return pages from freed allocations to the OS, rate-limited by a cooldown and guarded by a one-time symbol probe; it reads its settings through the explicitly *no-deepcopy* config loader because generating a full-config deepcopy per attempt would allocate exactly the garbage the module exists to release. A safe no-op on other platforms and allocators. (memory.mem-trim)
